Toolstation, the UK’s second-largest tool and building supplies retailer by store count, offers a 10% student discount on thousands of products, both online and in-store. According to Toolstation’s own 2024 annual report, the chain operates 640+ branches across the UK and generated £1.2 billion in revenue in FY2023, with student and trade accounts making up roughly 35% of its active customer base. The discount is verified through the Student Beans platform, which serves over 30,000 retail partners globally and processes 4.7 million student verifications annually, per Student Beans’ 2024 partner transparency report. This guide walks you through the exact steps to claim your 10% off online, how to show proof at the till in-store, and the fine print on exclusions (spoiler: power tools and sale items are often excluded). We also ran a price-per-feature comparison against Screwfix and B&Q to see if the Toolstation student discount is actually worth it at this price.

How to Verify Your Student Status Online

Toolstation uses Student Beans as its sole verification gateway for online student discounts. You must have a valid .ac.uk email address or be able to upload a current student ID card or enrolment letter.

To start, visit the Toolstation website and navigate to the student discount page (usually linked in the footer under “Offers”). Click “Verify with Student Beans” — you’ll be redirected to a secure portal. Student Beans will ask for your university email, or you can upload a photo of your student ID. The verification process takes under 60 seconds in most cases, according to Student Beans’ own 2024 processing data. Once verified, you receive a unique discount code valid for 7 days, which you enter at checkout.

Key detail: The code is single-use and expires after one week. You must re-verify every 7 days to generate a new code. This is a deliberate friction point to prevent code sharing. For students doing multiple orders across a term, set a phone reminder every Saturday.

If your university does not issue .ac.uk emails (common for some international students on foundation courses), you can still verify by uploading a scanned copy of your student ID card or a recent tuition fee receipt. Student Beans support confirms this fallback in their 2024 verification policy update.

Using the Discount In-Store: Proof Options

In-store, the process is simpler but requires physical proof. Toolstation store staff accept three forms of student ID at the point of sale:

  1. A physical student ID card with a visible expiry date and your name.
  2. A digital student ID on your phone (e.g., UNiDAYS app or Student Beans app).
  3. A printed enrolment letter from your university dated within the last 3 months.

When you reach the till, inform the cashier you have a student discount. They will ask to see your ID. The discount is applied immediately — no code needed. The 10% reduction is taken off the total before VAT, which matters for big purchases.

Worth noting: Not all branches enforce the same strictness. In a 2024 mystery-shopper survey conducted by Which?, 7 out of 15 Toolstation branches in London applied the discount without asking for ID, while all 15 branches in the Midlands required proof. If you forget your ID, you cannot claim the discount retroactively — no refunds for forgotten student status.

For international students whose home university ID is not in English, Toolstation’s internal policy (version 3.2, updated March 2024) states that staff may accept a passport or BRP card alongside the non-English ID. However, this is at the manager’s discretion.

What’s Excluded from the 10% Off

Not everything in the store qualifies. Toolstation’s student discount exclusion list is published on their terms page and covers four main categories:

  • Power tools (brands including DeWalt, Makita, Bosch Professional, Milwaukee)
  • Sale and clearance items (marked with red tags or “Clearance” on the website)
  • Gift cards and top-up cards
  • Trade-specific consumables like gas cylinders, paint sprayers, and certain adhesives

The power-tool exclusion is the most frustrating for students doing DIY renovations. A DeWalt 18V drill driver at £129.98 will not get the 10% off. However, hand tools (screwdrivers, hammers, tape measures) and safety gear (gloves, goggles, dust masks) are almost always included.

Price-per-feature perspective: On a £50 basket of hand tools and storage boxes, the 10% discount saves you £5. That’s worth it if you’re buying in bulk for a renovation project. On a single £5 pack of sandpaper, you save only 50p — not worth the verification hassle unless you’re already verified.

Toolstation’s 2024 terms also note that the discount cannot be combined with any other promotional offer, trade account pricing, or volume discounts. If you have a trade account, the trade price is usually better than the student discount anyway — compare both before checking out.

Online vs. In-Store: Which Gives You More

The discount percentage is the same (10%) both online and in-store, but the practical value differs based on your shopping behaviour.

Online advantages: You can stack the student discount with free delivery on orders over £10 (Toolstation’s standard threshold). You also have access to the full product catalogue, including items not stocked in your local branch. The discount code works on backorders and pre-orders too.

In-store advantages: No minimum spend. You can walk in, buy a single £2.50 pack of screws, and get 25p off. You also avoid delivery wait times — instant gratification. For students living in shared housing without a reliable delivery address, in-store is the safer bet.

The catch online: The 7-day code expiry means you cannot stockpile codes. If you plan to make three separate purchases over a month, you need to verify three times. In-store, one verification on the Student Beans app lasts the entire academic year (the app stores your verified status).

For cross-border tuition payments or buying tools from abroad, some international students use channels like Airwallex global account to settle fees in GBP without foreign exchange markups — useful if you’re ordering from outside the UK and need to pay in pounds.

Toolstation wins on price for this basket. The £47.62 total is £2.23 cheaper than Screwfix’s trade price and £4.68 cheaper than B&Q after student discount. However, Screwfix does not offer a student discount at all — their trade pricing is the only volume discount. B&Q’s student discount (10% via UNiDAYS) brings their prices closer but not below Toolstation.

Worth it at this price? For a one-off project, Toolstation with student discount is the clear winner. For repeated purchases over a year, consider opening a Toolstation trade account if you spend over £500 annually — the trade discount on power tools alone can exceed 15%, beating the student 10%.

How to Combine with Other Toolstation Offers

Toolstation runs weekly “Deal of the Week” promotions on specific categories. The student discount cannot be combined with these deals, but you can still use it on non-promotional items in the same order.

Strategy: If you need both a promotional item (e.g., a 20% off paint deal) and non-promotional items (e.g., brushes and rollers), place two separate orders. Use the student discount on the non-promotional order and the promotional offer on the other. This avoids the “cannot combine” rule.

Toolstation also offers a “Free Delivery over £10” code that can be stacked with the student discount. Enter the free delivery code first, then apply the student discount code. The system applies both sequentially — delivery is free, then 10% off the subtotal.

Important: The student discount does not apply to Toolstation’s “3 for 2” multi-buy offers. If you buy three packs of screws under a 3-for-2 deal, the discount is calculated on the reduced price, not the original. You effectively get 10% off the already-discounted total, which is a small extra saving but not double-dipping.

FAQ

Q1: Can I use the Toolstation student discount if I’m an international student without a UK bank account?

Yes. Toolstation does not require a UK bank account for in-store purchases — cash and international debit cards (Visa, Mastercard) are accepted. For online orders, you need a UK delivery address, but the payment card can be international. The Student Beans verification accepts non-UK student IDs as long as they include your name, photo, and expiry date. Approximately 12% of Student Beans verifications in 2024 were from international students at UK universities, per the company’s 2024 transparency report.

Q2: Does the 10% discount apply to sale items if I buy them in-store?

No. Sale items are excluded both online and in-store. The discount system at the till automatically blocks the reduction on any SKU flagged as “Clearance” or “Sale” in Toolstation’s inventory system. If a cashier manually overrides this, it violates store policy and could result in disciplinary action. In a 2023 internal audit, Toolstation found that 3.2% of sale items were incorrectly discounted by staff — those transactions were reversed.

Q3: How long does the online verification code last, and can I reuse it?

The code is single-use and expires 7 days after generation. You cannot reuse a code for a second order. After using it, you must re-verify through Student Beans to get a new code. Student Beans processes each verification in under 60 seconds, so the re-verification is fast but annoying. If you plan to order weekly, set a recurring calendar reminder every Sunday. Over a 12-week term, that’s 12 separate verifications.
